note: Made the way 1 John 2 was redone on 2026-11-21: every idea has its own present-day symbolic picture, arriving with the sentence it shows, each made wide (1920x1088) and tall (1088x1920) from the same description. A scene starts at the first word of its verse, or at its "from" words inside the verse. For text that is hard to picture: the text's own image moved into today; else what the idea does in a life today; else keep the previous picture. Such scenes carry "hard": true and a "hard_note". After the ideas were written each one was checked again against 'is this the best possible picture for what these verses mean?'. Biblical people are not portrayed (verse 12 names Cain) and nothing violent is shown.

scenes.principle: We are called his children, and we are. That is the kind of love we have been given.
scenes.shows: A very small child's hand wrapped around his father's finger as they walk.
scenes.prompt: Close view from behind and low down of a very small child's hand wrapped tightly around one finger of his father's much larger hand as the two walk together along a garden path. Only the two joined hands, the child's small arm and a little of each of them are in frame, the hands in sharp focus. Soft, bright overcast morning light.

scenes.principle: We are children now. What we will be is not yet seen, but we will be like him.
scenes.shows: A small boy stands in his father's big work boots.
scenes.prompt: A small boy of about four in pyjamas stands in the hallway of a home with both feet inside his father's huge, worn leather work boots, which reach almost to his knees. He looks down at them with a delighted, serious face. A man's work jacket hangs on a hook above him. No adult is in the picture. Clear, even daylight from an open doorway to the side.

scenes.principle: Whoever holds this hope makes himself clean, to be like the one he hopes to see.
scenes.shows: A young man washes his face with clear water in the morning.
scenes.prompt: A young man in a plain white T-shirt bends over a simple white bathroom basin and lifts both cupped hands, full of clear running water, to wash his face. Drops of clear water catch the light. Seen from the side. Fresh, bright early-morning light from a window. No mirror writing, no bottles with labels.

scenes.principle: Sin is lawlessness: it runs straight through what the law says.
scenes.shows: A car runs a red light at an empty crossing.
scenes.prompt: An ordinary city crossroads at blue hour just after sunset, wet road. A traffic light glows clearly red in the foreground, in sharp focus, while a dark car speeds straight through the crossing beneath it, blurred by its speed, its tail lights streaking. No other cars. There are no road signs, no signboards and no lettering anywhere, and the driver cannot be seen.

scenes.principle: He came to take sins away, and in him there is none. Whoever stays in him is not ruled by sin.
scenes.shows: Two hands lift a heavy, muddy pack off a worn-out hiker's back.
scenes.prompt: On a steep mountain trail at midday under a high clear sky, an exhausted hiker in ordinary outdoor clothes stands bent forward with his hands on his knees. Behind him a second person, seen only as two strong arms and hands reaching in from the edge of the frame, is lifting a huge, heavy, mud-caked rucksack up and off the hiker's shoulders. The straps are just coming free and the hiker is beginning to straighten.
scenes.hard_note: 'Take away sins' has no picture of its own today. This shows what it does: a load lifted off. Verse 6 has no honest picture, so this one stays up through it.

scenes.principle: Do not be fooled: the one who is right with God is the one who does what is right.
scenes.shows: A man hands a dropped wallet back to its owner.
scenes.prompt: A busy but softly blurred city pavement in plain afternoon daylight. A man in an ordinary jacket has caught up with a stranger and is holding out a brown leather wallet to her; the surprised woman, turning back, is just reaching to take it with a grateful look. The wallet between their hands is in sharp focus. The wallet is plain, with no lettering.

scenes.principle: Sin is the devil's work, and the Son of God came to undo it.
scenes.shows: A heavy chain lies broken on the ground, its padlock open.
scenes.prompt: A heavy, rusted iron chain lies on bare ground, snapped clean apart, its broken link in sharp focus, and beside it a large old padlock lying sprung open. Behind, out of focus, an iron gate stands wide open onto a sunlit field. Cool shade in the foreground, bright clear late-morning light beyond the gate.

scenes.principle: Whoever is born of God carries his nature inside, and what is inside decides what grows.
scenes.shows: An acorn has split and a small oak shoot grows from it, a great oak behind.
scenes.prompt: Extreme close view at ground level of an acorn lying on dark, damp soil, split open, with a small pale root going down and a young green shoot with two tiny oak leaves rising from it. Far behind, soft and out of focus, stands a great old oak tree. Gentle, even light under a bright overcast sky.

scenes.principle: God's children are known by this: they do what is right and they love their brother. It is the message from the beginning.
scenes.shows: A boy kneels to tie his little brother's shoelace.
scenes.prompt: On the front steps of an ordinary school on a clear weekday morning, a boy of about ten with a school bag on his back kneels on one knee and carefully ties the shoelace of his little brother of about five, who stands holding on to his big brother's shoulder for balance. Plain everyday clothes. Clean, even morning daylight.

scenes.principle: Hatred of a brother grows from resenting the good he does. The world resents it in the same way.
scenes.shows: One brother is praised at the family table while the other stares down, jaw tight.
scenes.prompt: A family dinner table at home in the evening under a warm ceiling lamp. On the right a young man smiles modestly while an older relative's hand, reaching in from the edge of the frame, rests proudly on his shoulder. On the left, in sharp focus, his brother, who looks much like him, sits apart with his arms folded, staring down at the table with a tight jaw and a dark, resentful look. Nobody else's face is visible.
scenes.hard_note: The text names Cain. Biblical people are not portrayed and nothing violent is shown, so this shows the resentment the verse gives as the reason.

scenes.principle: Love for the brothers is how we know we have crossed over from death into life.
scenes.shows: A footbridge leads from a burnt, grey wood into living green.
scenes.prompt: A narrow wooden footbridge crosses a small ravine, seen from the side. On the left bank stands a burnt, dead forest of black, leafless trunks on grey ash. On the right bank the forest is alive, green and sunlit, with ferns and wildflowers. A walker with a small rucksack, seen from behind, is just stepping off the bridge onto the green side. Bright, clear midday light.

scenes.principle: To hate a brother is to do away with him in your heart, and no life remains in that.
scenes.shows: An old photograph of two brothers, torn in two between them.
scenes.prompt: An old, slightly faded colour photograph of two young brothers standing side by side lies on a dark wooden table, torn in two straight down the middle between the boys, the two halves lying a little apart with rough torn edges. The torn photograph is in sharp focus. Cool, grey window light from one side. No writing on the photograph. Apart from the two boys in the photograph there are no people in the frame.

scenes.principle: This is how we know love: he laid down his life for us. We ought to do the same for one another.
scenes.shows: A firefighter walks alone into the smoke of a burning house.
scenes.prompt: A firefighter in full, plain dark protective gear and helmet, seen from behind, walks steadily and alone up the path toward the open front door of an ordinary house from which thick grey smoke is pouring. Everyone else has left; the firefighter is the only person in the frame and is going in. No flames are visible, only heavy smoke and a faint orange glow deep inside the doorway. Flat grey overcast daylight. No lettering, numbers or badges on the gear or anywhere else.

scenes.principle: If you have plenty, see your brother in need and shut your heart to him, how can God's love be living in you?
scenes.shows: A well-dressed man with full shopping bags walks past a man sitting in the cold, looking away.
scenes.prompt: A city pavement on a cold, bright winter afternoon. A man in a worn coat sits on the ground against a wall with a blanket over his knees, looking up. A well-dressed man in a good wool coat, carrying several full, plain shopping bags, walks past him close by with his face turned firmly away. The seated man is in focus; the walker is caught mid-stride. The bags are plain with no logos or lettering.

scenes.principle: Love is not talk. It is something done.
scenes.shows: Someone kneels and wraps a warm coat around the same man's shoulders.
scenes.prompt: The same kind of cold, bright winter pavement. A man in a worn coat sits on the ground against a wall. A passer-by in a jumper has knelt down in front of him and is wrapping their own thick winter coat around the seated man's shoulders with both hands. The seated man looks up in surprise. The kneeling person is seen from behind and the side.

scenes.principle: When our own heart accuses us, we can rest before him, because God is greater than our heart and knows everything.
scenes.shows: A child who has broken a vase is held close in his father's arms.
scenes.prompt: A living-room floor in soft afternoon window light. In the foreground lie the pieces of a broken vase and some scattered flowers on wet floorboards. Just behind, a father kneeling on the floor, seen from behind, holds his small son close in both arms; the boy, in focus, presses his tear-streaked face into his father's shoulder with his eyes shut. The father's face is not visible.
scenes.hard_note: An accusing heart and its reassurance are inward things. This shows them in a home: the one who knows exactly what happened holds the child anyway.

scenes.principle: A clear heart comes to God boldly, asks, and receives.
scenes.shows: A little girl holds her cup up high and it is being filled.
scenes.prompt: A little girl of about four stands on tiptoe in a sunny kitchen, holding a plain empty cup up as high as she can with both hands and looking up with complete trust and a wide smile. From the top edge of the frame an adult's hand tips a clear glass jug, and a stream of clear water is pouring into her cup. Only the adult's hand and forearm are visible. Bright, clean mid-morning light.

scenes.principle: His one commandment has two sides: trust in his Son, and love one another.
scenes.shows: A family and friends join hands around a dinner table to give thanks.
scenes.prompt: Close view along an ordinary dinner table set with a simple home-cooked meal, in warm early-evening lamp light. People of different ages sit around it with heads bowed, holding one another's hands in an unbroken ring around the table. The joined hands resting on the tablecloth in the foreground, an old hand holding a child's hand, are in sharp focus, and the faces are soft and out of focus.
scenes.hard_note: 'Believe the name of his Son' has no picture of its own. This shows the two sides of the command as one everyday act: thanks given together, hand in hand.

scenes.principle: Whoever keeps his commandments lives in him, and he in them. We know he lives in us by the Spirit he gave.
scenes.shows: A small house at dusk with its windows glowing and smoke rising from the chimney.
scenes.prompt: A small, plain house stands alone on a snowy hillside at deep blue dusk. Every window glows with warm golden light, and a thin line of smoke rises straight up from the chimney into the still, cold air. Fresh footprints in the snow lead up to the front door. You can tell at a glance that someone lives there. No people are visible.
scenes.hard_note: 'Remains in him, and he in him' is the language of living in a home. This shows how you know a house is lived in: by the light and the warmth inside.

method: Second method, asked for by Obay on 2026-11-21 after the sentence-by-sentence pictures did not connect: (1) split the chapter into sections that each carry one deep meaning, written as one plain sentence; (2) write 10 different picture ideas for each section; (3) judge them: which shows the deep meaning most truly, then which a watcher understands at once while hearing the words, then which is most engaging; (4) make the top two for each picture slot as real pictures ("candidates") and choose by eye. A section has one or two pictures. What he said went wrong before: he could not tell why some pictures were there, could not connect them to the meaning, and some were too abstract.

sections.meaning: God's love has made us his children. That is who we are now, and we are growing to be like him.
ideas: A small boy runs in through an open front door into waiting arms
A very small hand wrapped around a parent's finger
A boy standing in his father's big work boots
A boy stretching against height marks on a door frame
A small girl held tight, her face peaceful over a shoulder
A boy copying his father shaving at the mirror
A new framed photo being hung on the family wall
Morning light falling on a child asleep, a hand tucking the blanket
A new small chair set at the family table
A sapling beside a great tree of the same kind

sections.meaning: Sin is rebellion against God, and Jesus came to take it away. A life in him and a life of sin do not go together.
ideas: Handcuffs fall open from a man's wrists, another hand holding the key
A stain washing out of a white shirt under clear water
A heavy muddy pack lifted off a hiker's back
A car running a red light
A wall of scrawl being painted clean
A man dropping a bottle into a bin and walking on
Rubbish bags carried out of a filthy room
A man walking out of a dark alley into a bright street
A chalkboard wiped clean
A mud-covered child laughing as he is hosed clean

sections.meaning: Do not be fooled: your life shows whose child you are. What you do again and again shows the family you belong to.
ideas: A small girl kneading dough exactly the way her mother does
A boy and his father walking with the same stride
A son sanding wood beside his father with the same motion
A man handing back a dropped wallet
An older brother wrapping his jacket around his little brother
A boy tying his little brother's shoelace
Old and young faces in profile with the same features
A man studying his own face in a mirror
A teenager alone at night doing the right thing unseen
A boy whose shadow on the wall has his father's shape

sections.meaning: Love one another. Hating a brother is death at work in you, and love is how you know you are alive.
ideas: One brother is praised while the other stares down, jaw tight
A man walks away from his brother's outstretched hand
A man asleep at his brother's hospital bed, holding his hand
Two brothers in a fierce embrace after years apart
A photograph of two brothers torn in two
A footbridge from a burnt wood into a green one
Two brothers back to back on either side of a shut door
An empty place at a family table
A clenched fist beside an open hand
A dead houseplant beside a living one

sections.meaning: Love is not talk. Love gives itself: he laid down his life for us, so we give what we have for one another.
ideas: A man wades through floodwater carrying an old man on his back
A firefighter walks alone into a smoking house
A lifeguard plunging into storm surf
Someone wraps their own coat around a man sitting in the cold
A workman breaks his sandwich and gives half away
A well-dressed man walks past someone in need, looking away
A kidney donor and the one who received it, hand in hand
A mother gives her child her own plate of food
A nurse asleep, worn out, at a patient's bedside
A stranger pays for the shopping of the person in front

sections.meaning: We can rest our hearts before God. He is greater than our guilt, he hears us, and he lives in us as we trust his Son and love one another.
ideas: A man on the edge of his bed lifts his face into the morning light
A woman praying with open hands and an unafraid face
A child who broke a vase held close anyway
A little girl holding her cup up to be filled
Family and friends joining hands around a dinner table
One candle lighting another in a circle of people
A small house in the snow with every window lit
Open hands, palms up, in a shaft of light
Friends walking with arms around each other's shoulders
Breath rising in cold morning air

candidates.prompt: Seen from inside the bright hallway of a home, looking out through the wide-open front door: a small boy of about five with a little backpack runs in from the doorstep with a huge, joyful smile and his arms flung wide, straight toward two pairs of open arms reaching out to him from the near edges of the frame. Only the adults' outstretched arms and hands are visible. Warm light from inside the house falls on the boy's face. Clear morning daylight outside.

A small boy of about five stands very straight with his back against a white door frame at home, heels together, stretching up as tall as he can with a proud, hopeful face and one hand flat on top of his head. On the frame beside and above him is a column of short pencil lines at rising heights, the highest far above his head. There are no numbers and no writing, only plain pencil lines. Bright clear daylight from a window.

Close view of a man's two hands lifting apart as a pair of steel handcuffs falls open and away from his wrists. A second person's hand, at the edge of the frame, holds the small key that has just unlocked them. The freed wrists and the open handcuffs in mid-fall are in sharp focus. A plain room with bright daylight from a window behind. No uniforms, badges or lettering.

Two hands hold a white shirt under a stream of clear running water in a white basin. A dark, muddy stain on the cloth is washing away, and the part already rinsed is brilliantly clean and white. Clear water, bright even daylight. No labels or lettering.

A kitchen worktop in bright morning light. A mother's flour-dusted hands knead a round of bread dough, and right beside them a small girl's hands knead a small piece of dough in exactly the same way, copying her. The girl, about five, standing on a stool, watches her mother's hands with deep concentration. The mother is seen only as hands, forearms and apron. A little flour hangs in the air.

A winter bus stop on a grey, frosty morning. A teenage boy wearing only a thin jumper is wrapping his own warm jacket around his small, shivering younger brother and zipping it up to his chin, and the little boy looks up at him. Both carry school bags. Flat grey daylight, their breath visible in the cold air. No signs or lettering.

Two grown brothers who look alike stand in a driveway on an overcast day. The one nearer the camera, in sharp focus, has turned his back on the other and is walking away with a hard, cold face and his fists pushed into his jacket pockets. Behind him, slightly out of focus, his brother stands with one hand still held out to him, open, his face hurt.

A hospital room in quiet early-morning light. A man lies asleep in the bed, pale but peaceful, and beside the bed his brother, who looks much like him, has fallen asleep in a chair, bent forward with his head resting on the mattress, still holding his brother's hand in both of his. The joined hands are in sharp focus. No screens with numbers and no lettering.

An airport arrivals hall, softly blurred. Two grown brothers who look alike grip each other in a fierce, long-awaited embrace. The one facing the camera has his eyes shut tight and tears on his smiling face. A dropped travel bag lies at their feet. Bright, even daylight from high windows. No signs or lettering.

A flooded residential street under a heavy grey sky. A man in ordinary soaked clothes wades waist-deep through brown floodwater toward the camera, carrying a frail elderly man on his back, the old man's arms around his neck. The carrier's face shows strain and determination. Rain is falling. Nobody else is in the frame. No signs or lettering.

A city park bench at a cool, bright noon. A workman in a dusty work jacket has broken his sandwich in two and is holding out the bigger half to a thin, poorly dressed man sitting beside him, who looks at it in surprise. The workman's open lunch box rests on his knee. The offered half sandwich between their hands is in sharp focus.

A bedroom at first light. A man in a T-shirt sits on the edge of his unmade bed with his elbows on his knees, his head just lifted from his hands and his tired face turned toward the window, as a broad band of warm morning sunlight comes in and falls across his face and chest, pushing the grey dimness of the room back. His expression is beginning to ease. Only sky and light are seen at the window.

A woman of about forty sits on a plain chair by a window with her eyes closed and her face lifted, her hands resting open and upturned in her lap, with a calm, confident, unafraid smile. Clear morning light from the window falls on her face and open hands. A simple, uncluttered room. No religious objects of any kind.

Outdoors at dusk, a small circle of ordinary people of different ages stands close together, each holding a plain white candle. In the centre of the frame, in sharp focus, one person's lit candle is tilting to light the unlit candle of the child beside them, the new flame just catching. The faces around are warmly lit by candlelight and softly out of focus. Deep blue evening sky. No religious symbols.
